newsitem.title: UK: Inchcape to sell Bain Hogg to Aon Corp.
newsitem.headline: Inchcape to sell Bain Hogg to Aon Corp.

text.p: International distribution group Inchcape Plc said on Tuesday it agreed to sell its insurance broking unit, Bain Hogg Group Plc, to U.S. group Aon Corp for 160 million stg cash. It also saw an exceptional loss of about 195 million stg related to the sale.
The company said it had previously believed that a demerger was the most likely route for the divestment of Bain Hogg.

"However, having secured a price significantly above the value we expect the market to place on the company if demerged, I am convinced that today's disposal to Aon represents the best value for our shareholders," the company said in a statement.
The demerger of Bain Hogg would have required a net cash contribution of 13 million stg to give it an appropriate capital base as an independent business, it said.
"The estimated 20 million stg provision for the restructuring of Bain Hogg announced at the interims will no longer affect shareholders," Inchcape added.
The company also said it would continue to have the benefit of Bain Hogg's brokerage services on a global basis.
Inchcape planned to use proceeds from the sale to reduce its borrowings.

Taking into account the sale of Inchcape Testing Services last week and Bain Hogg, the company said its pro forma gearing would have been about five percent based on its June 30 balance sheet compared to the reported 74 percent.
Inchcape planned to complete the transaction on October 18.
"Today's announcement completes the process of focusing Inchcape as an international distribution group well within the timescale we outlined in March," the company said.
Bain Hogg had first-half operating profits of 20.8 million stg, down from 25.9 million stg in the year-earlier period.
The unit's turnover was 127.2 million stg in the first half of the year, compared to 123.3 million stg.
